The phenomenon of target radar cross section dependence on transmitted frequency was investigated as a candidate technique for target classification.
The experimental 94 GHz radar system was designed and built to obtain data for corner reflectors at various range spacings.
Theoretical computer simulations were developed and compared to the experimental data.
The frequency diverse bandwidth required to see one complete oscillation in V(f) is 15.0 MHz for a reflector separation of 10 meters.
The range separation between the two corner reflectors in the first experiment was 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 meters.
The power output of the 94 GHz radar transmitter was about 200 mW.
The sensitivity of the square law detector in the 94 GHz radar receiver was about 600 mV/mW.
The frequency of the 140 GHz radar was 142.02 GHz.
The pulse repetition interval of the 140 GHz radar was 33.3 usec.
The duty cycle of the 140 GHz radar was 9%.
The frequency diversity bandwidth of the 140 GHz radar was 660 MHz.
The range cell of the 140 GHz radar for a 3-usec pulse was 1500 ft.
The range cell of the 140 GHz radar for a 50-nsec pulse was 25 ft.
The 94 GHz radar system used a continuous wave (CW) klystron with a nominal power of 300 mW.
The 94 GHz radar system used a thermistor for monitoring the power.
The 94 GHz radar system used a cavity wavemeter for ballpark frequency measurements.
The 94 GHz radar system used a square law detector for monitoring the transmitted power waveform.
The 94 GHz radar system used a low noise preamplifier with a gain of ten and an input impedance of 1 MegOhm.
The 94 GHz radar system used a low bandwidth (500 KHz) high sensitivity (100 mV/division) oscilloscope.
The 94 GHz radar system used a boxcar averager/gated integrator with a variable size aperture.
The 140 GHz radar system used a coherent/pulse compression operating frequency of 142.02 GHz.
The 140 GHz radar system used a transmitted peak power of 10 mW (10 dBm).
The 140 GHz radar system used a pulse repetition interval of 33.3 usec.
The 140 GHz radar system used a duty cycle of 9%.
The 140 GHz radar system used a frequency diversity bandwidth of 660 MHz.
The 140 GHz radar system used a range cell of 1500 ft for a 3-usec pulse.
The 140 GHz radar system used a range cell of 25 ft for a 50-nsec pulse.
